seed.relationship: a brother and sister reading their mother's letters
seed.conflict: about a debt neither will mention
seed.topicSeed: a beekeeper's yard in Tehran; a brother and sister reading their mother's letters about a debt neither will mention

g.passage:
Tehran in late May, and the yard hums
the way our mother's kettle hummed before it boiled.
Pouya lifts each frame toward the light,
counts the capped cells aloud, names the queen
the way she named her hens, after aunts.
I read him her letters from the cedar box:
the price of sugar the winter I was born,
a neighbor's wedding, the plum tree she swore
she would graft and did, the next spring,
wearing her blue scarf against the wind.
Then the page about the shop.
I read the date.
I read the weather.
Pouya sets the frame back gently.
He asks for the next letter, please,
and thanks me when I give it,
and fills the smoker with dry pine needles
until the yard goes grey and quiet.
Leila, he says, read the plum tree again.
I keep my thumb on the third line
of the page about the shop, where her hand
leans the way it leaned when she wrote out sums.
g.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text and its significance?
options: It narrows from easy description to polite requests, suggesting Pouya wishes to show his sister more courtesy than before.
It narrows from fond, detailed memory to guarded brevity, suggesting both siblings are steering around a matter the letter raises.
It narrows from fond, detailed memory to guarded brevity, suggesting the speaker has grown tired of reading aloud to Pouya.
It narrows from fond, detailed memory to guarded brevity, suggesting the siblings have begun to quarrel over their mother's past.
g.explanation: 앞부분은 긴 행과 촘촘한 세부(설탕 값, 결혼식, 자두나무)로 어머니의 편지를 다정하게 읽지만, '가게에 관한 페이지'에서 행이 짧아지고 날짜와 날씨만 읽힌다. Pouya는 공손하게 다음 편지를 청하고 연기로 마당을 덮으며 자두나무 이야기로 돌아가려 하고, 화자는 숫자를 적던 필체의 줄에 엄지를 올려 둔다. 두 단서를 합치면 남매가 그 페이지가 꺼내는 문제(돈 문제)를 함께 피하고 있다는 B가 정답이다. A는 겉의 공손함만 읽었고, C는 원인을 화자 자신의 피로로 돌렸으며, D는 조용한 회피를 다툼으로 과장했다.

seed.conflict: about whether a small kindness was a cover for something else
seed.topicSeed: a rooftop laundry line in Albuquerque; two estranged sisters about whether a small kindness was a cover for something else

g.passage: “Hand me the blue pins, if you would,” Lakshmi said, and I did, and for an hour we worked the line on the roof of our mother's old boardinghouse in Albuquerque as if no years stood between us. She showed me how to shake a sheet so the wind takes the creases, how to hang shirts by the hem so the shoulders do not pucker, how the adobe parapet holds the morning heat like a palm. She had brought ironed handkerchiefs for me, a dozen, each with my initial stitched in the corner. I thanked her. She asked whether the deed to the house was still kept in the hall desk. I said that it was. We hung the pillowcases. We hung the towels. I thanked her again for the handkerchiefs. That evening I took the deed from the hall desk and carried it to my room, and I folded one of her handkerchiefs around it before I set it beneath my pillow.
g.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text and its significance?
options: It moves from practical lessons to repeated thanks, suggesting the narrator has grown more grateful for her sister's care.
It moves from easy fellowship to guarded politeness, suggesting the narrator regrets having said so little about the house.
It moves from easy fellowship to guarded politeness, suggesting the narrator suspects the gift served to ease a request.
It moves from easy fellowship to guarded politeness, suggesting the narrator has decided to cut off contact with Lakshmi.
g.explanation: 앞부분은 빨래 너는 법을 길고 구체적으로 묘사하며 자매가 가까워진 듯 보이지만, 집 문서에 관한 질문 뒤로 문장이 짧아지고 같은 감사 인사만 반복된다. 화자가 그날 밤 문서를 자기 방으로 옮기고 언니의 손수건으로 감싸 베개 밑에 두는 행동은 선물과 문서에 대한 질문을 연결해 의심을 드러낸다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 반복된 감사라는 겉 어조만 읽었고, B는 원인을 화자 자신의 침묵으로 돌렸으며, D는 조용한 경계를 절연으로 과장했다.

seed.relationship: a returning soldier and his younger sister
seed.conflict: about what to tell a younger sibling
seed.topicSeed: a bus depot in Dakar; a returning soldier and his younger sister about what to tell a younger sibling

g.passage: What does one say to a brother who has been gone three years? At the depot in Dakar I said nothing useful. I asked Kofi about the ship, and he told me everything: the salt crust on the rails, the cook who sang in Wolof and burned the rice, the porpoises off the cape that the men counted like coins. He laughed often. He asked after our mother, the goats, the mango tree by the well. Then I mentioned that our little brother Chinedu had practiced a salute for him all week. Kofi said that was kind. He said he would like to see it. He picked up his kit bag. On the bus he sat by the window and asked about the price of millet. When we reached the house and Chinedu ran out, standing very straight with his hand at his brow, Kofi knelt, folded the boy's raised hand down into his own, and held it there.
g.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text and its significance?
options: It changes from casual chatter to formal politeness, suggesting Kofi has resumed the manners his family expects at home.
It changes from lively storytelling to measured courtesy, suggesting Kofi is ashamed of having talked so long about himself.
It changes from lively storytelling to measured courtesy, suggesting Kofi is angry that Chinedu was taught to salute him.
It changes from lively storytelling to measured courtesy, suggesting Kofi is uneasy about being honored as a soldier.
g.explanation: 배 이야기를 할 때 Kofi는 소금기, 요리사, 돌고래까지 세세하게 말하며 자주 웃지만, 경례 이야기가 나온 뒤에는 짧고 예의 바른 말만 하고 화제를 기장 값으로 돌린다. 마지막에 그가 무릎을 꿇고 동생의 경례하는 손을 내려 자기 손에 쥐는 동작이 그 원인을 드러낸다. 즉 그는 군인으로 존경받는 일 자체가 불편한 것이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 겉의 공손함만 읽었고, B는 원인을 자신의 수다로 돌렸으며, C는 부드러운 만류를 분노로 과장했다.

seed.relationship: an elder and a restless apprentice
seed.conflict: about an ending that nobody wants to admit
seed.topicSeed: a kite-maker's yard in Lyon; an elder and a restless apprentice about an ending that nobody wants to admit

g.passage: Armand had built kites in the yard behind the old silk quarter of Lyon for forty years, and each morning he tested the frames before Okja arrived, bending every spar against his knee and listening for the small dry crack that meant bad wood. Lately he had begun leaving the spars in a heap for her to test alone. Okja took this as impatience. She tested them quickly, tossed the cracked ones aside, and asked for harder work: the great silk dragon for the midsummer festival, the commission he had promised the mayor. Armand said she might begin it. He watched her cut the first panel. That afternoon a carter came for the old drying racks, and Armand counted coins into the man's palm, and the man asked whether the yard would open again in spring. Armand told him to mind the gate. Okja kept cutting silk. When the light failed, he lit the lamp and set it beside her, and went inside without taking his own stool.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It begins with a habit the apprentice misreads, then shows a sale that recasts that habit, and ends with the question left unspoken.
It begins with the elder's morning routine, then describes the apprentice's eagerness, and ends with her request for harder work.
It begins with a habit that reveals the elder's plans, then shows the apprentice taking it as impatience, and ends with the question unspoken.
It begins with a habit the apprentice takes as impatience, then shows a sale that recasts it, and ends with the yard passing to her.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 Armand가 살대 검사를 Okja에게 맡기는 습관을 그녀는 조급함으로 읽는다. 중간에 건조대를 팔고 봄에 다시 열지 묻는 질문을 피하는 장면이 나오면서, 그 습관이 가게를 닫을 준비였음을 다시 읽게 된다. 마지막의 등불과 놓고 간 의자는 아무도 그 끝을 말하지 않은 채 장면을 열어 둔다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, B는 전반부만 요약했고, C는 재해석의 순서를 뒤집었고, D는 열린 결말을 해결로 오독했다.

seed.conflict: about an object that belonged to someone gone
seed.topicSeed: a crowded wedding hall in Haifa; a stepfather and his stepdaughter about an object that belonged to someone gone

g.passage: Noa hated weddings. In the hall in Haifa the band played too loud and the aunts pressed honey cake on anyone who sat down, and Yoav, her stepfather, moved through the crowd in a suit slightly too big in the shoulders. __He had worn the same wristwatch every day since she was nine, an old steel one that ran four minutes slow and that he never reset.__ Noa watched him dance with the bride's grandmother, then with a cousin, then with no one, swaying alone near the cake table with his eyes closed. She ate two pieces of honey cake. She checked her phone. At midnight, when the room counted down to the cutting of the cake, Yoav's voice came a little behind everyone else's, as if he were counting by another clock. Afterward he found her by the coat racks, unbuckled the watch, and fastened it on her wrist. Her father's initials were scratched into the back.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It presents a quirk that mainly establishes Yoav as careless about small practical matters.
It presents a quirk that later marks the watch as a keepsake of Noa's father.
It presents a quirk that explains why Yoav sways alone near the cake table at the wedding.
It presents a quirk that illustrates how weddings stir up old habits among the guests.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로 읽으면 늘 늦게 가는 시계를 고치지 않는 Yoav의 버릇을 묘사하는 배경 설명처럼 보인다. 그러나 자정 카운트다운에서 그의 목소리가 늦게 나오는 장면과, 시계 뒷면에 Noa 친아버지의 이니셜이 새겨져 있다는 마지막 사실이 이어지면 시계가 떠난 사람의 유품이었음이 드러난다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 B처럼 복선 기능을 한다. A는 밑줄만 단독으로 읽었고, C는 바로 뒤 장면과 연결해 해소로 읽었으며, D는 지문 표현을 빌려 지나치게 일반화했다.

seed.topicSeed: a seed-saving cooperative in Port of Spain; a grandmother and her grandson after an unsent apology

g.passage: Who labels seeds in pencil anymore? My grandmother Cecile did, every packet in the cooperative's back room in Port of Spain, in a slanted hand that faded within a year. __She said ink was for things a person was sure of.__ I spent that August sorting bodi beans and pigeon peas beside her, sealing envelopes, writing dates. She talked about rainfall and weevils and the price of jute sacks. She did not talk about my mother, who had not come home in six years. On the last day, reaching for a fresh box of envelopes, I found one already sealed and addressed in pencil to my mother in London, the stamp gone pale with age. Cecile took it from me, looked at it a long while, and slid it back into the box among the seed packets.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It offers a stated rule that later accounts for a letter written and kept back.
It offers a stated rule that mainly characterizes Cecile as a careful keeper of seed records.
It offers a stated rule that introduces the cooperative's practice of dating every packet.
It offers a stated rule that reflects the cooperative's caution about the uncertain rainfall.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 처음에는 연필로 이름표를 쓰는 할머니의 습관을 설명하는 성격 묘사처럼 읽힌다. 그런데 할머니가 딸 이야기를 피한다는 중간 단서와, 연필로 주소를 쓴 채 봉인되어 오래 보관된 편지가 발견되는 끝 장면이 이어지면, 이 말은 할머니가 확신하지 못해 보내지 못한 사과를 설명하는 복선이 된다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 밑줄만 단독으로 읽었고, C는 바로 뒤 문장(날짜 쓰기)과의 관계로 읽었으며, D는 지문 어휘(rainfall)를 빌려 일반화했다.

seed.relationship: a teacher and a student who will not speak
seed.conflict: after a teacher's remark that changed everything
seed.topicSeed: a train compartment in Mumbai; a teacher and a student who will not speak after a teacher's remark that changed everything

g.passage: Hari had not spoken to me since the morning I called his essay too careful to be brave. __On the train to Pune he took the upper berth and spread his notebooks across it, the way he used to spread them across the front desk of my classroom.__ The compartment filled with the smell of cardamom tea and wet umbrellas. A family below us argued over a tiffin of lemon rice. I graded papers. Hari watched the rain streak the window, and when the vendor came through he bought two cups of tea, set one on the ledge near my elbow without a word, and climbed back up. Near Lonavala the train stopped in a cutting. I looked up. Every notebook on the berth lay open, turned toward me, and on the top page, in his cramped hand, was a new first line, crossed out and rewritten four times.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes a habit that mainly shows Hari's wish to keep his distance from his teacher.
It describes a habit that later reads as a silent offer to share his work.
It describes a habit whose tension is resolved when Hari leaves a cup of tea for her.
It describes a habit that reflects how students carry the classroom into daily life.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로 보면 Hari가 위 칸에 올라가 거리를 두는 장면 묘사처럼 보인다. 그러나 끝에서 공책이 모두 선생님 쪽으로 펼쳐져 있고 네 번 고쳐 쓴 첫 문장이 보이는 장면이 나오면서, 공책을 펼쳐 놓는 옛 습관이 말없이 글을 보여 주려는 제안이었음이 드러난다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 밑줄만 단독으로 읽었고, C는 바로 뒤 차 장면에서 갈등이 해소된 것으로 읽었으며, D는 교실이라는 지문 표현을 빌려 일반화했다.

seed.relationship: a sister and her younger brother's tutor
seed.conflict: while one of them is pretending not to be proud
seed.topicSeed: a shoe repair stall in Bologna; a sister and her younger brother's tutor while one of them is pretending not to be proud

g.passage: Beside the shoe repair stall under the arcades of Bologna, Shuang waited each Saturday while the cobbler resoled whatever her family had worn through that week. __Chulsoo, her younger brother's tutor, passed the stall at nine o'clock exactly and lifted his hat to her without slowing.__ She considered him a stiff young man who corrected grammar at dinner. One Saturday the cobbler handed her the boy's boots and remarked that the tutor had paid for them already, as he had the month before. Shuang said that was unnecessary. She paid again, and the cobbler shrugged and pocketed both coins. The following week her brother brought home a prize for Latin composition, and Chulsoo, at dinner, remarked only that the ablative was still weak. At nine the next Saturday Shuang stood at the stall. The tutor lifted his hat, and his step, for once, slowed.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It introduces a routine that mainly establishes the tutor's formal and punctual manner.
It introduces a routine that confirms Shuang's sense of him as a stiff young man.
It introduces a routine whose stiffness later appears to mask his care for the boy.
It introduces a routine that reflects the polite customs of the city's busy arcades.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로 보면 Chulsoo의 딱딱하고 시간을 엄수하는 성격을 보여 주는 묘사다. 그러나 그가 몰래 동생의 구두 값을 두 번이나 치렀다는 사실과, 상을 받은 뒤에도 '탈격이 약하다'고만 말하는 태도, 마지막에 걸음이 느려지는 장면이 이어지며 그 형식적 태도가 자부심과 애정을 감추는 겉모습이었음이 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 밑줄만 읽었고, B는 바로 뒤 문장과의 관계로 기능을 뒤집었으며, D는 장소 표현을 빌려 일반화했다.

seed.conflict: over a plan that depends on a lie

g.passage: Chlorine and salt stung Dana's eyes the first morning at the pool in Vermont, and he complained about it to anyone who would listen, mostly Casey, his grandfather's old friend, who swam laps there at six. Casey talked too much, Dana decided. He told the same stories about the quarry, he whistled through his teeth, and he had a plan: they would tell Dana's grandfather the doctor said swimming would help his knee. The doctor had said no such thing. Dana told Casey it was a ridiculous plan. He went along with it anyway, which was not lying, exactly, he told himself, only agreeing in a loud voice. By the third week the grandfather was swimming. Dana came early now. He set Casey's towel on the warm bench by the heater, and when Casey told the quarry story again, Dana asked a question about the part he already knew.
g.question: Which choice best describes Dana's attitude toward Casey as conveyed in the text?
options: Mild contempt for Casey despite some patience with his repeated stories.
Quiet affection for Casey despite a habit of grumbling about him.
Guilty fondness for Casey despite private doubts about their shared plan.
Amused tolerance for Casey despite finding his plan rather ridiculous.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 Dana는 Casey가 말이 많고 같은 이야기를 반복한다고 불평하지만, 중간의 '정확히 거짓말은 아니'라는 자기 정정은 그가 Casey의 계획에 사실상 동참했음을 보여 준다. 뒤에서는 일찍 와서 Casey의 수건을 따뜻한 벤치에 놓고, 이미 아는 대목을 일부러 질문하며 이야기를 들어 준다. 말투와 행동의 어긋남을 합치면 B가 정답이다. A는 말투만 읽었고, C는 애정의 이유를 자신의 죄책감으로 돌렸으며, D는 지문 어휘(ridiculous)를 빌렸지만 행동 단서와 맞지 않는다.

seed.conflict: about the cost of a scholarship or opportunity
seed.openingStyle: 과거를 회상하는 문장으로 시작('Years later', 'Once' 등)
seed.topicSeed: a tea plantation in the Cornish coast; a captain and a stowaway about the cost of a scholarship or opportunity

g.passage: Once a month I brought the supply boat into the cove below the tea terraces, and that spring I found Mio curled behind the fertilizer sacks, a scholarship letter for a college in Plymouth folded in his shoe. I told him he was a nuisance. I told him stowaways ate more than paying cargo and complained about the smell of diesel, which he did, constantly. I made him scrub the deck twice a day. He asked what the fare would have cost. I said more than he had, which was not lying, exactly, only rounding up. On the last run before term I kept the boat in the cove an extra hour while he said goodbye to the pickers on the terraces, and I wrote nothing in the log about the extra fuel. When he asked again about the fare, I talked about the tide tables until he gave up.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Mio as conveyed in the text?
options: Weary impatience with Mio despite brief moments of shared humor aboard.
Protective care for Mio despite a wish to make up for her own past.
Quiet generosity toward Mio despite a show of gruff annoyance with him.
Grudging acceptance of Mio despite calling him a nuisance to the crew.
g.explanation: 화자는 앞에서 Mio를 골칫거리라 부르고 갑판 청소를 시키는 등 퉁명스러운 말투를 보인다. 중간에 뱃삯에 대해 '거짓말은 아니고 반올림했을 뿐'이라는 정정이 나오고, 뒤에서는 작별 인사를 위해 배를 한 시간 더 머물게 하고 연료 기록을 남기지 않으며 뱃삯 이야기를 피한다. 이 행동들은 말투 아래의 조용한 너그러움을 보여 주므로 C가 정답이다. A는 말투만 읽었고, B는 지문에 근거 없는 화자 자신의 과거를 이유로 들었으며, D는 지문 어휘(nuisance)를 빌렸지만 행동 단서를 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: a ferryman's daughter and a passenger
seed.conflict: over an invitation one of them refuses
seed.topicSeed: a school gymnasium in Chicago's South Side; a ferryman's daughter and a passenger over an invitation one of them refuses

g.passage:
By seven the gym on Seventy-First smells of floor wax
and the folding chairs are already crooked.
Devon, who rode my father's ferry every summer
and talked the whole way across about nothing,
asks me to the spring dance under the dead scoreboard.
I tell him he dances like a dropped mop.
I tell him I have a shift on the dock,
which is not lying, exactly—
my father would let me off if I asked.
He laughs. He says, Kenya, fair enough.
After he goes I stack the chairs he knocked over
and straighten the ones he didn't,
and when the custodian kills the lights
I stand a while by the bleachers
where he left his jacket, and fold it
sleeve over sleeve, the way my father folds a flag,
and carry it home on the ferry, on my lap,
the whole way across.
g.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Devon as conveyed in the text?
options: Teasing scorn for Devon while granting that he takes refusal well.
Fond regard for Devon while feeling bound by duty to her father.
Amused patience for Devon while finding him talkative about nothing.
Hidden tenderness for Devon while turning him away with jokes.
g.explanation: 화자는 Devon이 '떨어진 대걸레처럼 춤춘다'고 놀리고 부두 근무를 핑계로 초대를 거절한다. 그러나 '정확히 거짓말은 아니'라는 정정으로 아버지가 쉬게 해 줄 것임을 스스로 인정하고, 뒤에서는 그가 넘어뜨린 의자를 정리하고 두고 간 재킷을 정성껏 접어 무릎에 올린 채 집까지 가져간다. 농담과 행동의 어긋남을 합치면 감춘 애정을 말하는 D가 정답이다. A는 말투만 읽었고, B는 거절의 이유를 아버지에 대한 의무로 뒤집었으며, C는 지문 표현을 빌렸지만 행동 단서와 맞지 않는다.

seed.conflict: over whether to tell the truth to a dying friend
seed.topicSeed: a ferry terminal in Thessaloniki; two strangers sharing a delay over whether to tell the truth to a dying friend

g.passage: What is owed to a stranger met in a delay? I put the question to myself at the ferry terminal in Thessaloniki, where the steamer was held two days by weather, and where a gentleman named Emre occupied the bench beside mine and would not stop talking. He was travelling to a dying friend. He talked of whether to tell the man that his son had lost the family vineyard, and he talked of it badly, in circles, through too much tobacco. I found him tiresome, and I said so to the clerk, which was not unkind, exactly, only accurate. On the second evening I bought two coffees and set one by his elbow. When he began again about the vineyard, I did not turn the subject, and I asked what his friend had loved most about the vines.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Emre as conveyed in the text?
options: Growing sympathy for Emre despite a stated weariness with his talk.
Mild disdain for Emre despite a polite tolerance of his company.
Kindly interest in Emre despite wishing mainly to pass the delay.
Tired impatience with Emre despite finding him less tiresome later.
g.explanation: 화자는 앞에서 Emre를 지루하다고 평가하고 직원에게까지 그렇게 말하지만, '불친절한 것은 아니고 정확할 뿐'이라는 자기 정정이 그 평가를 누그러뜨린다. 뒤에서는 커피를 사서 그의 팔꿈치 옆에 두고, 포도밭 이야기를 피하지 않은 채 친구가 무엇을 사랑했는지 묻는다. 이 행동은 말투 아래 공감이 자라고 있음을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 말투만 읽었고, C는 관심의 이유를 지루함 달래기로 돌렸으며, D는 지문 어휘(tiresome)를 빌렸지만 행동 단서와 맞지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a foreman and a young hire
seed.conflict: when the plan works and nobody feels better
seed.topicSeed: an apartment stairwell in Lisbon; a foreman and a young hire when the plan works and nobody feels better

g.passage: Yona ran the crew that rewired the old apartment block in Lisbon, and on my first day he told me I held a screwdriver like a soup spoon. He said that sort of thing all spring. He timed my coffee breaks. He called me the intern in front of the tenants, though I was nothing of the kind. His plan was to finish the stairwell before the inspector came, working nights, and it worked: the inspector signed off on a Friday, and nobody on the crew so much as smiled. I told my sister he was impossible, which was not quite fair, I suspected even then. On the last night I stayed after the others, coiled the leftover cable the way he coiled it, elbow to thumb, left it on his toolbox with the ends taped, and went down the stairs without switching on the new lights.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Yona as conveyed in the text?
options: Lingering resentment of Yona despite relief that the job is finished.
Unspoken respect for Yona despite complaints about his harsh manner.
Dutiful gratitude to Yona despite doubts about her own skill at work.
Weary tolerance of Yona despite finding him impossible at times.
g.explanation: 화자는 앞부분에서 Yona의 조롱과 휴식 시간 재기 같은 거친 태도를 나열하고 동생에게 그가 '불가능한 사람'이라고 말한다. 그러나 '그다지 공정하지 않았다'는 자기 정정이 이어지고, 마지막 밤에는 그가 하던 방식대로 전선을 감아 끝을 테이프로 감싼 뒤 그의 공구함에 남겨 둔다. 그의 방식을 따라 하는 이 행동은 말하지 않은 존경을 드러내므로 B가 정답이다. A는 불평의 말투만 읽었고, C는 이유를 자신의 실력에 대한 불안으로 돌렸으며, D는 지문 어휘(impossible)를 빌렸지만 행동 단서와 맞지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a teenage cook and her stern aunt
seed.conflict: over a shared chore that has become a ritual
seed.topicSeed: a bakery before opening in Chengdu; a teenage cook and her stern aunt over a shared chore that has become a ritual

g.passage: Four rules governed the bakery in Chengdu before dawn: flour first, then water, then salt, then silence. Dalia had learned them at fourteen, when her aunt took her in, and for three years the two of them had folded dough side by side without speaking, her aunt's knuckles pressing a pattern that Dalia copied stroke for stroke. Each morning her aunt set out two aprons on the counter, though Dalia owned three of her own. Dalia never asked why. That winter her aunt's wrists swelled, and one morning she did not come down. Dalia worked alone. She weighed the flour, poured the water, measured the salt. When the first trays were out, she found that she had set two aprons on the counter herself, and that between folds she had been pausing for knuckles beside hers that did not come. She took the second apron and hung it back on its hook.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The text shows how a strict aunt trains her niece in a craft through wordless repetition.
The text shows how a young cook manages the bakery alone while her aunt is unwell.
The text shows how a silent chore became a bond felt most in its absence.
The text shows how working alone leads a young cook to take up her aunt's routine.
g.explanation: 앞부분(사건 1)은 이모와 Dalia가 말없이 반죽을 접는 엄격한 일과를 보여 주고, 이유가 설명되지 않는 앞치마 두 장이 중간에 미해결 디테일로 남는다. 뒷부분(사건 2)에서 혼자 일하게 된 Dalia가 스스로 앞치마 두 장을 꺼내고 곁의 손을 기다리며 멈추는 모습은, 그 일과가 단순한 훈련이 아니라 둘의 유대였음을 다시 읽게 한다. 따라서 두 사건의 관계를 진술한 C가 정답이다. A는 사건 1만, B는 사건 2만 말했고, D는 일과가 이미 있었는데도 혼자 일한 것이 그 원인인 것처럼 인과를 뒤집었다.

seed.relationship: a keeper and a visiting surveyor
seed.conflict: while one of them prepares to leave for good
seed.openingStyle: 과거를 회상하는 문장으로 시작('Years later', 'Once' 등)
seed.topicSeed: a rooftop water tank in Nairobi; a keeper and a visiting surveyor while one of them prepares to leave for good

g.passage: Years later the tenants of the block in Nairobi would still describe Ren tapping the rooftop water tank each dawn with a spanner, three knocks, listening for how full it rang. Moshe, the surveyor sent by the water board, watched him do it on his first morning and noted in his ledger that the meter had been broken for a decade. Ren nodded. He showed Moshe where the overflow pipe rusted, where pigeons drank, where the children hid their kites. In a corner of the roof sat a folded canvas bag that neither man mentioned. On Moshe's final morning he brought a new meter, installed it, and read the numbers aloud. Ren listened, then picked up the spanner, knocked three times on the tank, and handed the spanner to the boy from the third floor who had come up to watch. Then he lifted the canvas bag onto his shoulder.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The text shows how a visiting surveyor learns that a building's meter has long been broken.
The text shows how a new meter gives the tenants a dependable reading of their water.
The text shows how a keeper's plan to leave prompts the water board to install a meter.
The text shows how a keeper hands on his skill as a device seems to replace it.
g.explanation: 앞부분(사건 1)에서 Ren은 고장 난 계량기 대신 물탱크를 두드려 수위를 듣고, 구석의 캔버스 가방은 설명 없이 남는다. 뒷부분(사건 2)에서 새 계량기가 설치된 뒤에도 그는 세 번 두드리고 스패너를 소년에게 건넨 다음 가방을 메고 떠난다. 두 사건을 합치면 기계가 그의 기술을 대체하는 순간에 그가 그 기술을 다음 사람에게 넘긴다는 D가 요지다. A는 사건 1만, B는 사건 2만 말했고, C는 떠남이 계량기 설치의 원인인 것처럼 인과를 뒤집었다.

seed.relationship: a young apprentice and a master carpenter
seed.conflict: over blame for a lost opportunity
seed.topicSeed: a roadside diner in Krakow; a young apprentice and a master carpenter over blame for a lost opportunity

g.passage: By the time we stopped at the diner outside Krakow, the commission was gone: the church restorers had chosen another workshop, and Matthias said it was because my joints on the sample pew had gapped. I agreed. I had measured too fast. Over pierogi and weak coffee he listed my errors, calmly, the way he listed lumber, and I wrote them on a napkin. On the windowsill beside our booth stood a small carved bird with one wing mended in a darker wood; neither of us spoke of it. A year later, sorting his papers when his eyes failed, I found the restorers' letter. They had praised the pew. They had chosen the other workshop because Matthias asked a price he must have known they could not pay. I drove out to the diner again. I ordered pierogi and weak coffee, and I left the napkin, still folded, under my cup.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: The text shows how a later discovery recasts a fault the narrator had once accepted.
The text shows how an apprentice learns from a careful list of her own errors.
The text shows how a letter reveals the restorers' high opinion of a sample pew.
The text shows how losing a commission leads a master to price his work too high.
g.explanation: 앞부분(사건 1)에서 화자는 일을 놓친 원인이 자신의 이음매라는 Matthias의 말을 받아들이고 실수 목록을 냅킨에 적으며, 고쳐진 나무 새는 설명 없이 남는다. 1년 뒤(사건 2) 발견한 편지는 의뢰를 잃은 진짜 이유가 Matthias가 일부러 높게 부른 값이었음을 드러내 사건 1을 다시 읽게 한다. 따라서 나중의 발견이 받아들였던 잘못을 다시 보게 만든다는 A가 요지다. B는 사건 1만, C는 사건 2만 말했고, D는 높은 가격이 의뢰를 잃게 한 원인인데 인과를 뒤집었다.
